description: FireSafetyNet is an image dataset for training computer vision models that detect and inspect fire safety equipment, such as extinguishers and their markings, inspection tags and fire class symbols, in buildings. It was published on Zenodo on 20 September 2024 by Angelina Aziz, Jan Hendrik Heinbach and Lukas Trost of Ruhr University Bochum, with a journal paper. Images were taken with mobile cameras in public buildings in Germany, including university buildings, student dormitories and shopping malls. The archive is split by task: equipment detection, marking detection, condition checks (modal and amodal, with validation data and pretrained weights) and extraction of details from inspection tags and fire class symbols. Coverage: public buildings in Germany. Access: eight ZIP files of between about 0.2 and 1.8 GB on Zenodo. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: images from the FireNet dataset used in the paper are excluded for licensing reasons and must be obtained from FireNet. Simulation uses: automated facility-management inspection and condition data for building digital twins. Related records: the CHAS heritage point clouds and the BOOSS thermal aerial dataset.
